source: The Century Dictionary and Cyclopedia (1897), vol. 1, p. xviii (Internet Archive centurydictionary01whit, leaf n25): KEY TO PRONUNCIATION, SIGNS
note: Each symbol is the Unicode a transcription must use for the printed mark, NFC-normalized; combining marks are written as escapes so no two look-alike characters can be confused. 'uncertain' marks a reading a proofreader should confirm against the page.

vowels.as_in: mute, acute, few (also new, tube, duty)

single_dot_under.meaning: a vowel in an unaccented syllable, abbreviated and lightened without absolute loss of its distinctive quality

double_dot_under.meaning: a vowel in an unaccented syllable whose sound is variable to, and in ordinary utterance becomes, the short u-sound (of but, pun)

breve_under.meaning: the consonants t, d, s, z variable to ch, j, sh, zh

consonants.mark: small capitals TH, the T barred

consonants.as_in: French nasalizing n, as in ton, en

accents.meaning: secondary accent (not marked at its regular interval of two syllables from the primary or another secondary)

signs.meaning: and; compounded with, or with suffix
theoretical or alleged; theoretically assumed, or asserted but unverified, form

superior_figures: A superior figure after a title-word marks a word distinct etymologically from others spelled the same: back<sup>1</sup>, back<sup>2</sup>†, back<sup>3</sup>.
